newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tanker trade slow, rates holding steady.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tanker trade slow, rates holding steady.

text.p: Dirty tanker chartering activity was slow in most regions on Monday with worldscale rates little changed, brokers said.
VLCCs continued to see moderate demand in the key Middle East Gulf region for voyages East, but brokers were pessimistic as to how long rates would hold steady.
"Unless demand improves rapidly, a growing flotilla of surplus tonnage will pressure rates," a broker said.
Apart from light demand in the West African market trade for Suezmax tonnage was slow. Aframax vessels saw more moderate demand but rates failed to improve.

VLCC fixings to the U.S. Gulf held steady W50 although trade in the direction has been fairly thin. Voyages to Singapore held W55 and S.Korea and Japan valued around W57 with 230,000 tonne to Japan taking W59.

Transatlantic trade from West Africa saw limited activity after some improvement in trade late last week. Rates for million barrel tonnage held around W92.5 for voyages to the U.S. Gulf with a vessel booked for voyage to NWE at a steady W100.
Med/Black Sea trade continued to see enquiry for cross-Med Aframax tonnage but actual bookings were slow.
120,000 tonnes was booked from Novorossiisk to UKC-Med at W90 and Aframax rates held around W92.50.

North Sea, Inter UKC trade for 80,000 tonne business was holding around Friday's lower levels after falling by around 30 points over the week as more ships were shown to slowing demand from charterers.
Rates for inter UK-Cont voyages held around W105.
